newsitem.title: USA: PrimeCo launches new PCS phone service.
newsitem.headline: PrimeCo launches new PCS phone service.

text.p: PrimeCo, a mobile telephone venture owned by AirTouch Communications Inc and three regional Bells, on Tuesday launched a new wireless service with monthly charges between $18 and $50, and phones for $199.
The tiny new phones come with caller ID, voicemail, call waiting, call logging, billing check and balance alert services. The last two allow users to manage their bill.

PrimeCo's owners, Bell Atlantic Corp, NYNEX Corp, U S West Communications Group as well as AirTouch in 1995 paid $1.1 billion in a Federal auction for a set of Personal Communications Services (PCS) licenses.
Reuters reported details of the launch on Monday.
PrimeCo says its PCS service offers crystal-clear connections, with few dropped calls and little static, and extended battery life compared with cellular services.
"It will attract former cellular customers who were not happy with their services as well as new users," PrimeCo chief executive Ben Scott told a news conference.
The first batch of phones are made by Qualcomm Inc, which also owns the Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) technology the network uses.

PrimeCo services are available from Wednesday in Chicago, in Richmond and Norfolk in Virginia, Houston, Dallas/Fort Worth, San Antonio and Austin in Texas, New Orleans in Louisiana, and all cities in Florida.
Two calling plans are available. Clearchoice.1, priced at $18-$30 dependent on the home state, has a per minute charge of 25-30 cents in that local calling area.
Clearchoice.100 has 100 free minutes a month, and costs from $35-$50 a month, with minutes in excess of 100 costing 19-26 cents each.
Mobile phones usually charge for inbound calls too. To encourage the use of its PCS phones to pick up inbound calls, PrimeCo allows a free first minute on each inbound call.

PrimeCo will operate 34 retail stores and 1-800 sales channel, and its products will also be available through retailers like Best Buy Co Inc, Circuit City Stores Inc, Computer City, Incredible Universe, Office Depot Inc and Tandy Corp's Radio Shack.
